Topics · Hard times

They say God needed my son. Is that true?

No one here says your son was needed elsewhere. A father who wept, mercy for the bereaved, no full answer.

If you are in pain right now, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, or to a local crisis line or emergency number. Find a helpline near you

Translation of the meaning

And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white[614] from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.[615] They said, "By Allāh, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or become of those who perish." He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allāh, and I know from Allāh that which you do not know.

Translator's notes

[614] i.e., he lost his sight. [615] He did not express the extent of his grief or his anger at what he suspected his sons had done but was patient, depending only upon Allāh for help.

Quran · Yusuf 12:84-86

Translation

I cry with my voice to Yahweh. With my voice, I ask Yahweh for mercy. I pour out my complaint before him. I tell him my troubles. When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you knew my route. On the path in which I walk, they have hidden a snare for me.

Original · Hebrew

ק֭וֹלִי אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֶזְעָ֑ק ק֝וֹלִ֗י אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃ אֶשְׁפֹּ֣ךְ לְפָנָ֣יו שִׂיחִ֑י צָ֝רָתִ֗י לְפָנָ֥יו אַגִּֽיד׃ בְּהִתְעַטֵּ֬ף עָלַ֨י ׀ רוּחִ֗י וְאַתָּה֮ יָדַ֪עְתָּ נְֽתִיבָ֫תִ֥י בְּאֹֽרַח־ז֥וּ אֲהַלֵּ֑ךְ טָמְנ֖וּ פַ֣ח לִֽי׃

the Psalms · 142:1-3

World English Bible

Start by saying what this app will not say: that your son was needed elsewhere. The Quran does not say it. What the Quran does is show a father who lost a son. His eyes whitened with grief. No one explains it to him. He does not pretend, and he does not turn away from the One he is speaking to.

A question for you

What would you want someone to say at your door?

If you sayNothing. Just to sit with me.
ThenThat is what the text does: it does not explain, and it lets the sorrow be spoken.
If you sayMy child's name.
ThenNames remain. Those who say them have a place in the next passage.
If you sayThat it was not my fault.
ThenMany parents ask this. The next passage speaks of mercy for the bereaved.

Translation of the meaning

And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient, Who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allāh, and indeed to Him we will return." Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:155-157

Translation

and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

Original · Hebrew

וְיָשֹׁ֧ב הֶעָפָ֛ר עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָ֑ה וְהָר֣וּחַ תָּשׁ֔וּב אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְתָנָֽהּ׃

Ecclesiastes · 12:7

World English Bible

This passage is honest: loss is part of this life, in fear, hunger, wealth, lives and fruits. It does not call the loss good. It turns to the one who bears it: glad news for those who stay steady and say, when struck, that to God they belong and to Him they return. Then comes something said directly to them: blessings and mercy from their Lord. The mercy is promised to the one who bears the loss, not to the loss.

A question for you

How does 'to Him they return' sound to you right now?

If you sayCold.
ThenIt may be. The passage does not ask you to feel otherwise today. It ends with mercy.
If you sayLike a door left open.
ThenThat is close to what the words mean: parting is not the end of the road.
If you sayI cannot hear it yet.
ThenThat is all right. The verse stays where it is until you can.

﴿قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ۚ لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ فِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ ۗ وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةٌ ۗ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّـٰبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say,[1345] "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allāh is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account [i.e., limit]."

Translator's notes

[1345] The Prophet (ﷺ) is instructed to say on behalf of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) to His believing servants.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:10

Translation

For even though the fig tree doesn’t flourish, nor fruit be in the vines, the labor of the olive fails, the fields yield no food, the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls, yet I will rejoice in Yahweh. I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!

Habakkuk · 3:17-18

World English Bible

One more line, for the long road. The patient are given their reward without measure. It does not say the grief is a price, and it does not say the loss was needed. It says that the one who keeps going, in a wide earth, in what is hard, is not forgotten, and that what is given back is beyond counting. The words are 'without account'. No one is tallying what you have lost against what you are owed.

A question for you

What helps you carry the days?

If you sayRoutine.
ThenRoutine can be a form of patience, and patience is what the verse speaks of.
If you sayPeople.
ThenPeople are one of the doors of mercy.
If you sayPrayer or silence.
ThenThat is what the father did in the first passage: he took his sorrow to the One who hears.

The same in the other books
